title: Intestinal inflammation targets cancer-inducing activity of the microbiota
central_claims: Inflammation alters microbiota and pks-positive E. coli promotes colon tumorigenesis; pks deletion reduces tumor multiplicity and invasion without reducing inflammation.

research.summary: Altered experiment timing and early mortality prevented interpretable replication of central tumorigenesis comparisons. Colibactin-producing E. coli promoted tumor growth via senescence and HGF in independent models. Cancer-associated E. coli promoted polyps in Min mice and was associated with adverse clinicopathology. Repeated pks-positive E. coli exposure induced a distinct human organoid mutation signature absent with isogenic mutants; the signature occurred in independent human cancer cohorts.
